census_limit: Exactly the one declared post-core current-process census. Afterward choose policy or stop the native gate; do not add loader traces, baseline runs, repeated censuses or compatibility forensics.
minimum_next_decision: Read the one complete, durable, untruncated census as a bounded consistency check; keep eligibility false in the census result.

If only declared self/core4 plus System32 platform context appears, select one policy and its assumptions before any next ABI run; platform-context policy is the proportional option when OS trust is accepted, finite pins remain an optional reproducibility requirement.
If census is incomplete or shows unexpected protected native/outside-platform modules, retain the failed gate rather than expanding OS diagnostics or broadening the list opportunistically.

Any chosen policy must be prospectively identical across child guard/header, parent validator, contract/input rules and protocol, with wrong-path/native-namespace/failure-vector review and separate root launch decision.

The next native objective stays the two typed version/default observations and later separately gated grammar correctness, with strict resource/Job/no-model/no-CPU controls; previous failures remain unchanged.
note: This scope addendum narrows the earlier future-eligibility discussion: basic finite pins may support reproducibility, but broad publisher authentication and shim/load-cause evidence are not prerequisites to an explicit trusted-platform assumption.
objective: Evidence proportionate to typed ABI/grammar correctness; no general OS authentication or shim-causation project.

options.benefit: Explicit current-host module/pin reproducibility; strongest continuity with existing finite list.
options.cost: Additional finite path/hash pins and coordinated header/parent changes; Windows startup/API-host variation may make names brittle.
options.minimum: Use the complete census set once, review all additions together, and only if needed perform one separately approved basic static pin batch. No recursive OS dependency/authentication exercise.
options.name: finite_reviewed_extra_System32_set

options.benefit: More proportionate when the trusted Windows host is already an assumption and the goal is core4 ABI/grammar behavior; avoids one-name-at-a-time OS retries.
options.boundary: Accept only normalized reported canonical-System32 DLL paths as platform context; exact self/core4 paths/pins remain, protected ggml/llama/CPU application namespaces and wrong-path core/libomp remain rejected, and all other outside-System32 modules remain rejected.
options.limits: Reported directory/name membership does not authenticate an image, prove unshimmed calls, explain a load or guarantee later/lifetime closure. No universal containment or zero-initializer-effects claim.
options.minimum: A complete census showing the declared self/core and platform-only boundary, followed by an explicit root acceptance of the host-OS trust assumption and coordinated source/parent/contract/protocol policy. No per-platform-DLL publisher/loaded-byte authentication is required for this narrower goal.
options.name: System32_as_explicit_platform_context
